newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss aluminium sector moderately optimistic in 97.
newsitem.headline: Swiss aluminium sector moderately optimistic in 97.

text.p: Switzerland's VSAI aluminium industry association said it was moderately optimistic for prospects in 1997 because the weaker Swiss franc had boosted export possibilities.

"The Swiss Aluminium industry, which employed around 10,000 people in 1996, looks to the future with moderate optimism," it said in a statement, noting that rising prices and increasing orders were brightening the mood.
"The positive correction of exchange rates should create good conditions primarily for exports," it said.

"In addition, positive indices in the sector are the generally reduced inventories, an upswing in prices on metals market and not least aluminium's innovative potential, especially in transport, where advances continue unabated."
VSAI said the domestic market for semi-finished products fell five percent in 1996 to 110,000 tonnes. Total net aluminium consumption slipped to 117,000 tonnes from 131,000 tonnes.
Exports on aluminium products by value were steady at 1.31 billion Swiss francs last year, while imports dipped around three percent to 881 million francs.
